text:
Asha: Quick sync — ran the multi-region latency sweep for model v2-quant8 across H100 / A100 / L4. Notable p50/p95 divergence when edge routing flips between 'latency-first' and 'cost-first'. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/bench/regions/1770456 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Ben: Can you paste the raw p50/p95 numbers? need breakdown by region + GPU to triage properly. :eyes:

Asha: Pasted top-line from perf-bot automated run (run-id 1770456):
perf-bot: H100 (us-east) — p50=18ms, p95=72ms; A100 (us-west) — p50=22ms, p95=120ms; L4 (eu-west) — p50=30ms, p95=210ms. Quant8 enabled, batching disabled for interactive profile.

Carlos: A100 p95 looks bad. Kernel selection? fallback to non-fused kernels?

Asha: Yes — H100 used fused-attn v3. A100 fell back to triton-gemm v1 for the final layers due to unsupported block size after quantization. We also observed ~4% KV-cache misses on the A100 shard because of placement skew.

Ben: That KV miss + fallback kernel would explain the tail. Also routing policy matters: when edge-routing is set to 'cost-first' we send more inference to eu-west L4 which boosts throughput but tanks p95 for global users.

Ben: Quick repro curl (to force cost-first routing):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'X-Edge-Route: cost-first' \n  -d '{"model":"v2-quant8","input":"hello"}'
```

Lina: I pulled traces for the same window — p95 correlates strongly with eu-west->us-east network tails when requests are routed cross-region. Adding edge-affinity for sessions cut p95 in us-east by ~28% in the A/B test.

Asha: Proposed actions: 1) For interactive tier, default edge routing -> latency-first. 2) For cost-sensitive background jobs, keep cost-first. 3) Short term: pin low-latency customers to H100-fused variant. 4) Carlos to investigate A100 kernel fallback + shard placement. 5) Ben to re-run quant profile on L4 (decode overhead check).

Carlos: I'll take kernel/shard action. Plan: run kernel autotuner across a sample shard of A100 nodes, and try alternative sharding (replicated last-n layers). Scheduling sweep for tomorrow.

Ben: Note: quant8 increased token throughput ~1.8x on L4 but adds ~1–2ms extra decode overhead; when combined with network tails it amplifies p95. I'll re-run with async decode off to measure pure model-side tail.

Lina: I'll run a 2h window with latency-first routing and keep detailed traces. Will log changes to the routing flag and post results.

Asha: Thanks — Ben/Carlos/Lina, please update this thread with results. If we get consistent improvement, we'll update defaults and roll a short blurb to eng-runtime. For immediate mitigation, I'm going to add a routing bypass for enterprise customers so they don't get routed to eu-west L4 for interactive sessions.

Carlos: scheduling the tuning job now. Will attach kernel perf logs here once done.

Ben: starting L4 quant reruns (will push perf-bot run-id when finished).

Lina: running latency-first test in 5m window, will monitor p50/p95 and trace ids. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: new-run 1770456123-result — artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/1770456/summary.json, flamegraphs and kernel traces uploaded.

Asha: Great. We'll regroup after the three tasks. Heads up — if kernel tuning isn't sufficient, we might need to temporarily disable quant8 on A100 until we fix fallback kernel path.

Lina: ack.

Ben: ack, will report numbers as soon as run completes.

Carlos: ack, will post timeline and blockers.
